lessons.title: L'automne arrive - nos observations
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe and identify signs that autumn is beginning in our environment

opening.activity: Circle time (5 min): Show summer photo of school yard. Ask 'Qu'est-ce qui est différent maintenant?' Look out window together. Point and name: 'C'est l'automne!'

main.activity: Autumn detective walk (25 min): Outside or window observation with clipboards. Students draw/circle autumn signs on observation sheet: leaf colors, temperature feeling, clothing changes, sky appearance. Practice saying 'Je vois...' for each observation. Create class autumn discovery chart with student findings.

closing.activity: Science circle (10 min): Students share one autumn sign they found. Teacher records on class chart. End with autumn observation chant: 'En automne, ça change, en automne, c'est différent!'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students recognize autumn changes they see walking to school or playing outside

lessons.title: Les feuilles commencent à changer
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe leaf color changes and understand that this is a natural autumn process

opening.activity: Leaf mystery box (5 min): Feel different colored leaves in box without looking. Describe textures. Reveal and name colors: 'rouge, jaune, brun, vert'.

main.activity: Leaf color investigation (25 min): Collect or observe leaves from different trees. Sort into color groups using sorting mats. Create leaf rubbings with different colored leaves. Discuss: 'Pourquoi les feuilles changent-elles de couleur?' Simple explanation: Trees need less water, leaves change color. Practice color vocabulary with leaf sorting games.

closing.activity: Leaf color parade (10 min): Students hold up leaves and march around saying color names. Create class 'autumn color tree' by taping sorted leaves to wall tree outline.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice leaf color changes on trees in their neighborhood and understand why it happens

lessons.title: Pourquoi les feuilles changent-elles?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that leaves change colors because they need less sun and water in autumn

opening.activity: Plant needs drama (5 min): Students act as trees. Feel warm 'summer sun' (warm hands), drink 'water' (pretend). Then feel less 'autumn sun' (cooler hands), less water. Show how 'tree' changes.

main.activity: Sun and water experiment (25 min): Compare two small plants - one with full sun/water, one with less. Observe leaves. Use flashlight as 'sun' and watering as 'rain'. Demonstrate how less sun/water makes leaves change color. Create simple before/after drawings. Practice vocabulary: 'Le soleil donne de la lumière. L'eau aide les plantes. En automne, moins de soleil, moins d'eau.'

closing.activity: Tree needs chant (10 min): Create actions for sun (arms up), water (wiggling fingers down), and leaf colors (color gestures). Sing simple song about tree needs changing in autumn.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand why trees in their yard look different and how sun and rain affect plants

lessons.title: Collection de feuilles scientifiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will collect, sort, and record autumn leaf observations using scientific methods

opening.activity: Scientist preparation (5 min): Put on 'scientist hats' (real or pretend). Learn scientist jobs: observe, collect, sort, record. Practice carrying collection bags and clipboards carefully.

main.activity: Scientific leaf collection (25 min): Outdoor collection with scientist clipboards. Find 3-5 different leaves per student. Return to classroom for scientific sorting: by color, by shape, by size. Create individual leaf collection sheets with drawing/taping leaves and simple recording (tally marks, basic words). Use magnifying glasses to observe leaf details. Practice scientific vocabulary: 'Ma collection a...' 'Je trie par couleur.'

closing.activity: Scientist sharing circle (10 min): Students present one interesting leaf from their collection. Teacher helps them use scientific language: 'Cette feuille est rouge et petite.' Display collections on science wall.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students learn how scientists collect and organize natural objects to understand patterns in nature

lessons.title: Il fait plus froid - mesurer la température
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe that autumn brings cooler temperatures and learn simple temperature measurement

opening.activity: Temperature detective game (5 min): Students put hands on different surfaces (metal, wood, paper) and describe feelings: 'froid, frais, chaud'. Practice temperature vocabulary with gestures (shivering, fanning).

main.activity: Temperature investigation (25 min): Use large thermometer to check indoor temperature, then outdoor temperature. Students predict which will be colder. Create temperature comparison chart with pictures (ice = very cold, sun = very hot). Test temperature of water in different containers (ice water, room temperature, warm). Students sort classroom objects by temperature feeling. Practice saying: 'C'est froid', 'C'est chaud', 'La température change en automne.'

closing.activity: Temperature song and movement (10 min): Sing song about autumn temperature changes with movements (shivering for cold, wiping sweat for hot). Create class temperature calendar to track daily weather.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice that they need different clothing for autumn weather and understand temperature changes

lessons.title: Les jours deviennent plus courts
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe that daylight hours decrease in autumn and understand this affects living things

opening.activity: Light and dark exploration (5 min): Use classroom lights to demonstrate 'long day' (lights on long time) vs 'short day' (lights on short time). Students experience how less light affects activities.

main.activity: Daylight investigation (25 min): Compare photos of school at same time in summer vs autumn - notice sky brightness differences. Use flashlights to demonstrate how sun gives us less light in autumn (hold flashlight farther away). Create 'daylight timeline' showing morning, noon, evening in summer vs autumn using pictures. Students draw what they do when it gets dark earlier. Practice vocabulary: 'Le jour est court', 'Il fait noir plus tôt', 'Nous avons besoin de lumière'.

closing.activity: Daylight changes song (10 min): Sing about how autumn brings shorter days and longer nights. Create movements for sun rising late and setting early. Start class daylight observation chart.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice they need lights on earlier at home and have less time to play outside after school

lessons.title: Les animaux se préparent pour l'hiver
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe how local animals begin preparing for winter through behavior changes

opening.activity: Animal preparation mime (5 min): Students act out how they prepare for cold weather (putting on coats, gathering warm clothes). Introduce: animals prepare too, but differently.

main.activity: Animal preparation observation (25 min): Watch videos or observe local animals preparing for winter. Focus on specific behaviors: squirrels gathering nuts, birds eating more food, some animals growing thicker fur. Create class chart showing 'How animals prepare': gathering food, growing warm fur, finding warm homes. Students draw their favorite animal preparation behavior. Role-play being different animals getting ready for winter.

closing.activity: Animal preparation parade (10 min): Students move like different animals showing preparation behaviors (squirrel gathering, bird eating, bear finding den). Practice saying: 'Les animaux se préparent pour l'hiver.'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students observe squirrels, birds, and other animals in their neighborhood preparing for winter

lessons.title: Les oiseaux et la migration
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that some birds fly south for winter and observe migration behaviors

opening.activity: Flying south demonstration (5 min): Students spread arms like wings and 'fly' from cold area of room (with fan or ice) to warm area (with heater or sunny spot). Feel temperature difference.

main.activity: Bird migration investigation (25 min): Watch videos of birds flying in V-formations going south. Use simple map to show north (cold) and south (warm). Students practice 'flying south' movements across classroom map. Compare birds that stay vs. birds that leave using picture sorting activity. Create migration journal with drawings of birds flying south. Practice vocabulary: 'Les oiseaux volent vers le sud', 'Il fait chaud au sud', 'Les oiseaux cherchent la nourriture'.

closing.activity: Migration flight simulation (10 min): Students line up in V-formation like migrating birds and 'fly' around classroom saying 'Nous volons vers le sud pour trouver la chaleur.' Create class migration chart.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice fewer birds in autumn and understand where they go for warmer weather

lessons.title: Fourrure d'hiver - les animaux qui restent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe how animals that stay develop thicker fur or change color for winter protection

opening.activity: Fur thickness exploration (5 min): Students feel different fabric samples (thin summer shirt vs thick winter coat). Discuss how thickness keeps us warm. Introduce: animals grow thicker fur the same way.

main.activity: Winter coat investigation (25 min): Compare photos of same animals in summer (thin fur) vs winter (thick fur). Use magnifying glasses to examine real fur samples or fabric samples of different thicknesses. Students sort animals into 'thick winter fur' vs 'thin summer fur' categories. Create thickness comparison using cotton balls (thin layer for summer, thick layer for winter). Practice saying: 'La fourrure épaisse protège du froid', 'Les animaux ont plus de fourrure en hiver'.

closing.activity: Fur protection dance (10 min): Students pretend to be animals growing thicker fur for winter - start thin and add imaginary layers. Practice fur vocabulary with actions (thick = arms spread wide, protect = arms around body).

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice their pets have thicker fur in winter or see wild animals with different coat thickness

lessons.title: Expérience: pourquoi la fourrure?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will conduct a simple experiment to understand how fur keeps animals warm in cold weather

opening.activity: Warmth prediction circle (5 min): Show ice cube and various materials (cotton balls, fabric, paper). Ask students to predict which will keep ice cube coldest longest. Explain: this is like fur keeping animals warm.

main.activity: Fur insulation experiment (25 min): Wrap identical ice cubes in different materials: bare (no fur), thin cloth (thin fur), thick cotton balls (thick fur). Place in cups and observe which melts slowest. Students make predictions, then check results every 5 minutes. Record observations with drawings and simple words. Alternative: Use thermometers in cups of warm water with different insulation to see which stays warmest. Create experiment recording sheet with predictions vs results.

closing.activity: Experiment conclusion sharing (10 min): Students share which insulation worked best and why. Connect to animals: 'Thick fur keeps animals warm like thick cotton balls kept our ice cold.' Practice scientific vocabulary: 'Notre expérience montre que...'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand why animals grow thicker fur and why people wear coats - both work as insulation

lessons.title: Nourriture d'automne - récolter et stocker
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand how animals collect and store food for winter when food becomes scarce

opening.activity: Food collection game (5 min): Scatter play food or pictures around room. Give students baskets and 2 minutes to collect as much as possible. Discuss: animals do this in autumn to prepare for winter.

main.activity: Food storage investigation (25 min): Watch videos of squirrels, chipmunks, and other animals collecting nuts and seeds. Set up classroom food storage activity: students sort play food into 'eat now' vs 'save for later' categories. Create storage containers with different foods. Discuss why animals store food (winter has less food available). Students draw animals collecting and storing food. Practice vocabulary: 'Les animaux récoltent la nourriture', 'Ils gardent la nourriture pour l'hiver'.

closing.activity: Food storage pantry tour (10 min): Create classroom 'animal pantry' with stored food pictures. Students take turns being different animals checking their food storage. Practice saying: 'J'ai assez de nourriture pour l'hiver.'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students observe squirrels burying nuts and understand why animals collect food when it's available

lessons.title: Notre jardin d'automne - que se passe-t-il?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe how garden plants respond to autumn changes and what happens to their growth

opening.activity: Plant life cycle review (5 min): Use actions to show plant growing from seed to full plant. Ask: 'What happens to plants in autumn?' Show wilted vs healthy plant examples.

main.activity: Garden change observation (25 min): Visit school garden area or examine potted plants showing autumn changes. Students observe and draw plants at different autumn stages: some still growing, some finished producing, some preparing for winter rest. Compare summer photos of garden to current appearance. Plant autumn seeds (lettuce, radish) in classroom containers to observe autumn growing conditions. Create garden observation journals documenting plant changes.

closing.activity: Plant needs discussion (10 min): Review what plants need (sun, water, warm weather). Discuss how autumn changes affect plant growth. Students predict what will happen to garden plants in winter.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand why family gardens look different in autumn and what happens to plants in colder weather

lessons.title: Expérience: les graines en automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will conduct experiments to understand how plants create seeds in autumn for next year's growth

opening.activity: Seed hunt introduction (5 min): Show various seeds (apple, bean, sunflower). Ask students to find seeds inside fruits/vegetables. Explain: plants make seeds in autumn so new plants can grow next year.

main.activity: Seed experiment setup (25 min): Students dissect autumn fruits/vegetables to find seeds (apples, pumpkins, peppers). Examine seeds with magnifying glasses and sort by size, shape, color. Plant different types of seeds in labeled containers with varying conditions (light vs dark, water vs no water). Make predictions about which seeds will grow best. Create seed experiment charts to track growth over time. Students draw the seeds they planted and write/dictate predictions.

closing.activity: Seed cycle song (10 min): Sing about how plants make seeds in autumn, seeds wait in winter, then grow in spring. Use actions for each part of seed cycle. Set up observation schedule for planted seeds.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand where seeds come from and how plants prepare for growing new plants next year

lessons.title: Notre livre scientifique d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a class science book documenting all their autumn observations and discoveries

opening.activity: Scientist author circle (5 min): Review all the autumn science discoveries made in previous lessons. Show real science books and explain: scientists write books to share their discoveries with others.

main.activity: Science book creation (25 min): Students work in pairs to create pages for class autumn science book. Each page covers one lesson topic (leaf changes, animal preparation, temperature, etc.). Include drawings, simple writing, photos from experiments, and key vocabulary. Students choose their best observations and discoveries to include. Teacher helps with writing and organization. Create table of contents and book cover with class input.

closing.activity: Book preview sharing (10 min): Each pair presents their favorite page from the science book. Practice using scientific language: 'Nous avons découvert que...', 'Notre expérience a montré...'. Plan book celebration for next lesson.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students learn how scientists document and share their discoveries just like authors write books

lessons.title: Prédictions: que va-t-il se passer en hiver?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use their autumn observations to make scientific predictions about winter changes (extension)

opening.activity: Crystal ball predictions (5 min): Use pretend crystal ball (clear bowl) to make silly predictions, then explain scientists make predictions based on what they observe, not magic.

main.activity: Winter prediction workshop (25 min): Review autumn observations from science book. Students make predictions about winter: What will happen to leaves? How will animals behave? What will the weather be like? How will plants change? Create prediction charts with drawings and simple explanations. Students share reasoning: 'Je pense que... parce que...' Compare different students' predictions and discuss possibilities.

closing.activity: Prediction time capsule (10 min): Students write/draw their winter predictions and place in class 'prediction box' to open in winter to check accuracy. Practice scientific prediction language.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students use their autumn observations to predict winter changes they'll see at home and school

lessons.title: Automne autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how autumn looks different in various climates and regions (extension)

opening.activity: World autumn tour (5 min): Show globe and explain autumn happens in different ways around the world. Point to local area and other regions while showing autumn photos from each.

main.activity: Global autumn exploration (25 min): Compare autumn in different places using photos/videos: deciduous forests (colorful leaves), evergreen forests (stays green), tropical areas (less obvious changes), desert regions (minimal changes). Students sort pictures into 'autumn like ours' vs 'different autumn'. Create world autumn comparison chart. Discuss why autumn looks different in different places (different trees, different weather).

closing.activity: World autumn celebration (10 min): Students choose their favorite type of autumn from around the world and explain why. Create classroom display showing different global autumn experiences.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand that autumn happens differently around the world but people everywhere notice seasonal changes

lessons.title: Expérience: créer de l'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will design experiments to recreate autumn conditions and observe their effects (extension)

opening.activity: Experiment designer introduction (5 min): Introduce students as 'autumn scientists' who will create autumn conditions in the classroom. Review what makes autumn different: less light, cooler temperature, less water.

main.activity: Create autumn experiment (25 min): Set up experiments to recreate autumn conditions: Place plants in different light conditions (full light vs reduced light), different temperatures (warm vs cool areas), different watering schedules (normal vs reduced water). Students predict what will happen to plants under different 'autumn' conditions. Create experiment tracking sheets and begin observations. Students design their own mini-experiments with teacher guidance.

closing.activity: Experiment prediction circle (10 min): Students share their experiment setups and predictions. Begin observation schedule for tracking changes over time. Practice scientific language: 'Si nous changeons..., alors...'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand how environmental changes cause the autumn effects they observe in nature

lessons.title: L'automne et les humains
lessons.oneGoal: Students will investigate how humans adapt their behaviors and activities for autumn changes (extension)

opening.activity: Human adaptation demonstration (5 min): Students show how they dress differently for autumn weather compared to summer. Discuss other changes families make for autumn (different foods, activities, schedules).

main.activity: Human autumn adaptation investigation (25 min): Create comparison chart showing how humans and animals both adapt to autumn: clothing vs fur, heated homes vs dens, storing food vs gathering food, different activities vs migration/hibernation. Students interview each other about family autumn changes. Create human adaptation timeline showing changes from summer to autumn to winter preparations.

closing.activity: Adaptation comparison celebration (10 min): Students present one way their family adapts to autumn and compare it to animal adaptations studied earlier. Create class display showing human and animal autumn adaptations.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students recognize how their families change routines, clothing, and activities for autumn weather just like animals adapt

lessons.title: Présentation scientifique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will present their autumn science discoveries to others using scientific language and evidence (extension)

opening.activity: Scientist conference introduction (5 min): Explain that scientists share their discoveries at conferences. Students will be scientists presenting their autumn research. Practice using scientific language.

main.activity: Science presentation preparation and delivery (25 min): Students prepare short presentations about their favorite autumn discovery using class science book, experiment results, and observations. Include props, drawings, or demonstrations. Practice using evidence to support statements: 'We observed...', 'Our experiment showed...', 'The evidence proves...'. Students present to small groups or whole class.

closing.activity: Science celebration (10 min): Celebrate all scientific discoveries made during the unit. Students vote on most surprising discovery, best experiment, and most interesting observation. Award 'scientist certificates'.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students learn how scientists communicate their discoveries to help others understand the natural world

lessons.title: Fête des petits scientifiques d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their autumn science journey with families by sharing experiments and discoveries (extension)

opening.activity: Science celebration setup (5 min): Students put on scientist hats and prepare to share their autumn learning journey with families. Review key discoveries and prepare materials for sharing.

main.activity: Family science celebration (25 min): Students guide families through science stations: leaf color experiment, temperature measurement, animal adaptation demonstrations, plant growth observations, autumn prediction sharing. Students explain their discoveries using scientific vocabulary and evidence. Families participate in simple experiments and ask questions about observations.

closing.activity: Scientist achievement ceremony (10 min): Celebrate student growth as autumn scientists. Present certificates recognizing specific achievements (best observer, creative experimenter, thoughtful questioner). Students share one thing they learned about autumn changes.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students proudly share their scientific learning with families, building community appreciation for science education and environmental awareness
